name: Two Pointers
description: Uses two indices moving through an array (usually from both ends or at different speeds) to solve problems in O(n) time without extra space. Commonly used for sorted arrays, pair-finding, and linked list cycle detection.

examples.title: Example 1: Two Sum (Sorted Array)
examples.explanation: Since the array is sorted, moving left increases the sum, moving right decreases it. Time O(n), Space O(1).

examples.title: Example 2: Remove Duplicates In-Place
examples.explanation: Slow pointer tracks the position to write the next unique element. Fast pointer scans ahead. Time O(n), Space O(1).

name: Sliding Window
description: Maintains a window (subarray/substring) that slides through the data structure, expanding and contracting based on a condition. Used for substring, subarray, and contiguous segment problems in O(n) time.

examples.title: Example 1: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
examples.explanation: Expand window with right pointer. When duplicate found, shrink from left until valid. Time O(n), Space O(min(m,n)).

examples.title: Example 2: Maximum Sum of Size K Subarray
examples.explanation: Maintain a fixed-size window. Add new element, remove the one leaving the window. Time O(n), Space O(1).

name: Prefix Sum / Prefix Array
description: Precomputes cumulative sums (or products) into an array so that range queries can be answered in O(1) time. Reduces range-sum problems from O(n^2) to O(n).

examples.title: Example 1: Range Sum Query
examples.explanation: prefix[i] stores sum of nums[0..i-1]. Range sum from left to right is prefix[right+1] - prefix[left]. Build O(n), query O(1).

examples.title: Example 2: Product of Array Except Self
examples.explanation: Left pass stores product of elements to the left. Right pass multiplies by product of elements to the right. Time O(n), Space O(1) excluding output.

name: Palindrome & String Manipulation
description: String problems involving palindrome checking, reversal, or character-by-character processing. Often solved with two pointers or by converting to arrays for manipulation.

examples.title: Example 1: Valid Palindrome (ignoring non-alphanumeric)
examples.explanation: Clean string first, then use two pointers moving inward. Time O(n), Space O(n) for cleaned string (or O(1) if processed in-place).

examples.title: Example 2: Longest Palindromic Substring (Expand Around Center)
examples.explanation: Treat each character (and gap between characters) as a palindrome center and expand outward. Time O(n^2), Space O(1).
